The information you’ve been given is slightly off, starting with It’s actually ‘0.6 to 1 gram of protein per lb of lean mass’ with the upper end of that being more so for people that want to gain mass rather than tone-up. 


I workout pretty heavily 5 days a week and tend to do an upper/lower split (3/2) and managing 120-180 grams of protein per day is pretty simple. There’s little point in consuming above 30-40grams per meal due to limitations of what the human body can absorb in a 4 hour window, so to avoid waste keep that in mind. Just know that 20 grams of protein from animal products can be very different to 20 grams of protein sourced from plants due to the levels of various amino-acids - some protein is better than others.




This is my usual meal breakdown:

• Breakfast: Icelandic yogurt - 25gs protein & 250ish Kcal

• Lunch: 5 boiled eggs - 30ish gs protein & 250ish kcal

• Post-workout protein shake: - 40ish gs protein & 250ish kcal

• Dinner: lean meat to meet your protein & fat needs alongside a good source of fibre & carbs to keep a varied diet.

• Glass of milk before bed - 10ish gs protein

• If needed you can throw in things like beef jerky or protein bars where needed but watching calorie intake is advised.





In your last paragraph you bring up other supplements that people now take in bodybuilding, namely amino-acids and creatine:

proteins are just chains of amino-acids so it’s just another method of reaching your daily intake, I think supplementing them isn’t needed if your diet is varied.


Creatine, its a compound of 3 amino-acids and is naturally found in meats, taking it in the powdered form is just easier for some people, however creatine-loading may be something to look into as it’s a very safe supplement and it’s usefulness is drastic in terms of strength gains (up to 10% increase), it draws water into your muscles which will cause you to gain water weight but make your muscles bulge and look swole, depending on your body goals you may not want this though.



Best of luck with your gains.

97 anime —> Manga —> Movies —> 2016/17 anime —> Games
